title: What a faith-based investor is thinking about the coming Anthropic IPO

content_html:
'It is not the savior of the universe': A faith-based investor's view on the Anthropic IPO

By Samuel O'Brient

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

Initial public offerings are not usually occurrences that stoke religious debate, but most companies that go public are also not tinkering with ideas about the nature of consciousness itself.

Maybe that is why Anthropic's S-1 prospectus invited comparisons to a religious text. Where SpaceX's IPO filing was a sci-fi manifesto, the Claude maker's document stirred a sense of religious fervor in some who parsed its 300 pages.

Robert Netzly, the CEO of faith-based investment firm Inspire Investing, is not among those who felt that way.

"Claude is not Jesus" Netzly told Business Insider. "It is not the savior of the universe."

Netzly's firm conducts a "moral audit" of every potential investment, a process that consists of screening companies to ensure that they align with biblically responsible investing standards. SpaceX stock didn't meet this criteria, largely due to xAI's lack of guardrails around graphic content creation.

When it comes to Anthropic, though, Netzly says Inspire feels better about it, at least for now.

"The jury's still out whether we would encourage people to invest in Anthropic's IPO, but at least in that particular category, they have restrictions and safeguards around pornographic content and keeping that off of their software," he told Business Insider. "That's a big deal for us, and it's those sort of things that we're looking at when we make investment decisions."

When Anthropic published its S-1 filing in October, many investors focused on the numbers it revealed. But for some, the unexpected biblical parallels stood out more, such as wanting to "bring forth an age of miracles" and referring, rather apocalyptically, to "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" posed by the technology it is creating.

Netzly said he finds this ironic, and he doesn't approve of the framing employed by Anthropic. That said, he also sees a potential motive behind it that some investors may have missed.

"I think what they're trying to say, in religiously robed rhetoric , is that they're trying to get people of faith to embrace AI because they probably realize that group is among the most skeptical about AI and the evils that it could produce."

He added that if that is indeed Anthropic's intention, he sees the value in it, and that other faith-based investors should always remain alert and vigilant when it comes to new technologies. In his view, it doesn't help anyone if only people with bad intentions harness the power of AI.

Netzly has previously written about the role that fear plays in investing, noting that it has become a factor in faith-based investing as new technology can be potentially destructive. However, he doesn't buy into the AI doomsday scenarios that have percolated recently.

"The Bible has a lot to say about fear," he said. "In our faith-based approach, we really encourage investors to keep that in mind. In this case, an AI 'Age of Ultron' scenario unfolding could be reality. That really could happen. But we also know that God controls the future. People would be foolish to plan for human extinction."

塞缪尔·奥布莱恩 (Samuel O'Brient) 是一位经验丰富的金融市场和商业记者，撰写的文章涉及经济、技术和公共政策等广泛主题。 在《商业内幕》中，他报道了重要的宏观和微观经济故事，包括顶尖经济学家和对冲基金经理的观点、首次公开募股失败、企业破产、迷因股票和卖空。 他还撰写有关加密货币、石油和房地产等其他市场的文章。他采访了许多市场上最有影响力的声音，从马克·赞迪和理查德·塞勒等顶级经济学家到丹尼·摩西、安德鲁·莱夫特、安东尼·斯卡拉穆奇、路易斯·纳维利尔和格兰特·卡登等著名投资者。福克斯的 LiveNOW、Taking Stock 和 Ticker News 等节目让塞缪尔讨论股市和经济发展。 他的报道曾被纽约时报 DealBook、彭博电台、福布斯、Entrepreneur、Gizmodo 和 TheFutureParty 引用。Samuel 最初在 InvestorPlace 工作，报道投资、零售交易和宏观经济趋势。 在加入 Business Insider 之前，他曾担任 TheStreet 的技术市场记者。 他毕业于莎拉·劳伦斯学院和都柏林三一学院。Samuel 的作品曾发表在 TipRanks、EV 和 Observer 等出版物上。 当他不追寻故事时，人们经常会发现他在逛书店和唱片店。 要联系 Samuel，请发送电子邮件至 sobrient@insider.com 或通过 LinkedIn 与他联系。 他还在《信号》中饰演塞缪尔·克莱门斯。
